title: Frank Christian and the old ragtime players compared with Rene and Louis
summary: He judges the old ragtime-jazz men like Frank Christian against Rene, Louis, Sam Morgan and King Oliver, saying each had a different style.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, how did those corner players you say in later years compare with people like Frank Christian and the real old timers from that era, before your time?

Oh, well, Frank Christian was a... I wouldn't have called him a... He was more of a straight man. Christian. Frank Christian was. He... He wasn't a... Compared to a man like... I'm gonna say, nah, nah, that's my view, viewpoint. I don't know, everybody thinks things different though, but you couldn't compare him with a man like... The boy we were just talking about, Kid Rene and Louie and Emmon Hart and trumpet players like that. You... He was in a different category, I'd say. I'd say, yeah. He was in a... Category like Nick LaRock, I'd say. You know, they played a different style of jazz than these men played. The style they played, we used to call that jazz ago, ragtime jazz. And... But that wasn't Dixieland, huh? I don't know, I don't think that was Dixieland because... It didn't have the style. I didn't think it was the style. I wouldn't call that... I'd call that ragtime the way they had the name foot in those days. It was ragtime jazz. And a man like Hardy and Rene and Sam Morgan and... Buck Johnson, King Oliver. All them fellas had a different style. I don't know, it was a style you would... A musician would like to hear. That's the style I liked. Some of them played corn style. Some of them played... Take Louis. The style he's playing today, I have records on where Louis satin in the middle of a corn band. But his style is the same way. And he was born with that style. And he never did change that style. So they all had different styles. Of course they called them ragtime musicians. I don't know, I just called them playing corn. So I wouldn't compare them fellas with these fellas. Of course I may be wrong, I don't know. That's the way that I felt about different musicians that I've heard and played. Of course I played with plenty of corn bands myself in them days. Because I just needed the money.
